Root cause traced to phishing-induced execution of a malicious, obfuscated PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. Cobalt Strike beacon established outbound C2 communication to 198.51.100.23 on TCP/443. (T1071.001)

Firewall rule deployed to block all inbound traffic from 10.0.5.14.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Office Application
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
    process: powershell.exe
    parent_process: outlook.exe
  detection:
    selection:
      - ParentImage|endswith: '\outlook.exe'
      - Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
      - CommandLine|contains: '-nop'
      - CommandLine|contains: '-w hidden'
      - CommandLine|contains: '-encodedcommand'
    condition: selection
  level: high
  tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1566.001

rule SuspiciousRundll32FromTemp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32.exe loading DLLs from common temporary directories"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $temp_path1 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" wide ascii
        $temp_path2 = "\\Temp\\" wide ascii
        $rundll32 = "rundll32.exe" wide ascii
    condition:
        $rundll32 and ($temp_path1 or $temp_path2)
}

rule SuspiciousRundll32FromTemp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32.exe loading DLLs from common temporary directories"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $temp_path1 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" wide ascii
        $temp_path2 = "\\Temp\\" wide ascii
        $rundll32 = "rundll32.exe" wide ascii
    condition:
        $rundll32 and ($temp_path1 or $temp_path2)
}
